issues.sym: Coolant drips or pink/blue crust at the front of the engine, a sweet smell, a low-coolant warning, or the engine running hot.
issues.why: A leaking water pump is the most reported problem on this generation of Countryman, often well before 60,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when cold and have the leak traced. Replace the pump before it causes overheating.

issues.sym: Check engine light, a coolant leak at the thermostat housing, the fans running on after shutdown, or the engine running hot or slow to warm up.
issues.why: The electronically controlled thermostat and its plastic housing fail or crack with age; owners report replacements at 23,000-80,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Replacing a failed thermostat and housing is routine, but don't let the engine overheat.

issues.t: Cracked oil filter housing leaking oil and coolant
issues.sym: Oil and coolant leaking at the front of the engine, a dropping coolant level, or oil-soaked wiring.
issues.why: The oil filter housing also contains an oil cooler and can crack or leak at its gaskets, letting both oil and coolant out.
issues.next: Have it fixed promptly; leaking oil can ruin the wiring harness and drive belt, and coolant loss can overheat the engine.

issues.sym: Whining, grinding or clunking from the front of the car that changes with speed, often around 100,000 miles.
issues.why: RepairPal lists front differential failure as a common problem on this Countryman, usually reported around 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the noise checked early and ask about the differential and transfer unit oil. Driving on a failing differential can lead to a much bigger repair.

issues.sym: Loss of power, hesitation, long cranking or a no-start, and a check engine light.
issues.why: The direct-injection pump on the turbo engine is a known failure item; owners report replacements around 40,000-90,000 miles.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure codes checked. Ask a dealer about any extended coverage before paying.

issues.sym: Oil leaking around the turbo, smoke, or lost boost and power; on high-mileage cars the turbo can fail.
issues.why: The turbo's oil supply pipe leaks at its connections and can clog with baked oil, starving the turbo.
issues.next: Replace a leaking or old feed line early; it costs far less than a turbo. Keep up oil changes.

issues.t: Oil leak from timing (VANOS) or oil pump solenoid
issues.sym: Oil drips at the front of the engine, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: The seals on the camshaft timing (VANOS) and oil pump control solenoids leak; MINI issued a service bulletin for the oil pump solenoid leak.
issues.next: Have the leak traced. Resealing or replacing the solenoid is usually a moderate job.

issues.sym: Rough running, shaking at idle, hesitation and a flashing or steady check engine light.
issues.why: Ignition coils and spark plugs on these engines fail and cause misfires, often between 50,000 and 80,000 miles.
issues.next: Get the misfire codes read. Replacing the bad coil and worn plugs usually fixes it; a flashing light means stop driving hard.

issues.sym: Oil seeping around the top of the engine and a burning-oil smell.
issues.why: The valve cover gasket hardens with age and leaks oil.
issues.next: Fix it before oil reaches the spark plug wells or hot exhaust parts.

issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from the engine bay, sometimes with coolant or overheating warnings.
issues.why: The electric auxiliary pump that cools the turbo has a circuit board that can overheat and smolder.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 12V-008 and 18V-248. A dealer replaces the pump free.

issues.sym: No warning sign.
issues.why: A protective plate near the high-pressure fuel pump may be missing, so a crash could damage the pump and leak fuel.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 18V-557. A dealer installs the plate free.

issues.sym: The engine can stall while driving.
issues.why: The crankshaft sensor had incorrect software and could misread engine position.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 18V-465. A dealer replaces the sensor free.

issues.sym: Clunking or loose-feeling steering.
issues.why: A steering tie rod may have been assembled incorrectly, leading to wear and possible breakage.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 19V-601. A dealer inspects and replaces parts free.

issues.sym: Oil or coolant leaking under the car, often between 50,000 and 100,000 miles.
issues.why: The oil filter housing on BMW's B48 2.0L turbo engine can crack, leaking oil and coolant.
issues.next: Have leaks checked early. The housing is under the intake manifold, so labor is high; compare dealer and independent quotes.

issues.t: Electric water pump or coolant hose failure (2.0L turbo)
issues.sym: Coolant puddles, a coolant warning, overheating, or reduced engine power.
issues.why: The electric water pump and coolant return hoses on the B48 2.0L turbo engine are known to fail.
issues.next: Stop driving if it overheats and have the cooling system pressure-tested.

issues.sym: A low-coolant or overheating warning, coolant needing frequent top-ups, and in some reports a failed head gasket.
issues.why: Owner complaints to NHTSA for this generation include coolant loss and overheating on both the 1.5L and 2.0L engines. Leaking pumps, hoses or housings are common causes.
issues.next: Never ignore a coolant warning. Have the system pressure-tested to find the leak before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Plug-in hybrid battery weld beads fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign.
issues.why: Loose welding beads could create a path between hybrid battery cells, risking a short circuit and fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V-490. A dealer inspects and replaces battery modules free.

issues.t: Plug-in hybrid battery debris fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign.
issues.why: Debris may have entered the high-voltage battery cells during production, which could cause a short circuit and fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V-601 and do not charge the car until the free repair is done.

issues.t: Passenger seat belt locking feature may release early (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign; it matters most when a child seat is installed with the belt.
issues.why: The passenger belt's automatic locking retractor may switch off before the belt fully retracts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V-554. A dealer inspects and replaces the retractor if needed.

issues.t: Integrated brake system may lose power assist (recall)
issues.sym: Brake or stability warning lights, a hard pedal and longer stops; ABS and stability control may not work.
issues.why: The integrated brake system can malfunction. It is covered by recalls 24V-104 and 26V-422.
issues.next: Drive gently to a dealer if the lights come on and check your VIN for both recalls.

issues.t: Brake control module motor welds can break (recall)
issues.sym: Brake warning lights, a harder pedal and longer stops, with possible loss of rear brakes and ABS.
issues.why: Welds in the brake control module servomotor may break.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-697. A dealer replaces the brake unit free.

issues.t: Front seat belt retractors may be damaged (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign.
issues.why: A torsion bar in the front seat belt retractors may have been damaged during production.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-616. A dealer replaces both retractors free.

issues.t: Rear door armrest may come loose in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign.
issues.why: A rear door armrest bracket may not be secured properly, so the armrest could detach or interfere with the side airbag.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-340. A dealer replaces the door panels free.

issues.t: Front body structure bolts not tightened (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign.
issues.why: Some bolts in the front body structure may not have been tightened properly, reducing crash protection.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-711. A dealer inspects and tightens the bolts free.
